summary: Jørn Borup (1966–2023) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Aarhus University (~1998–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, later serving there as Associate Professor (~2008–2023).

Jürgen Hanneder (born 1964) is an Indologist who studied at Munich, Bochum, Bonn, and Marburg (PhD ~1993–1996), under Alexis Sanderson and Michael Hahn. His career includes posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1998–2007) and Marburg (Professor from 2007).

Jürgen Renn (born 1956) works in philosophy and history and archaeology. Educated at FU Berlin, Sapienza, and TU Berlin (PhD ~1987), he held posts at Boston University, became Director at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (1994), and joined MPI Geoanthropology (2022).

K. A. Nilakanta Sastri (1892–1975) was an Indian historian and Indologist. Educated at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras (~1911–1913), he held academic posts at Annamalai University (~1947–1952) and the University of Mysore (~1952–1956).

K. A. Subramania Iyer (1896–1980) was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He served as a Professor at the University of Lucknow (attested 1972) and as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
K. Kanapathypillai (1902–1968) was an Indologist and linguist. He received his education at Hartley College and the University of London (~1936–1940), and he taught Alvappillai Veluppillai.

K. Kunjunni Raja (1920–2005) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned PhDs at the University of Madras under C. Kunhan Raja and at SOAS/University of London under John Brough, later serving as Reader at Madras and honorary director of Adyar Library (~1980–2005).

K. L. Dhammajoti (born 1949) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Kelaniya under Yin Shun and Y. Karunadasa. He taught at Kelaniya (~1985–2004) and held posts at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and HKU.

K. Meenakshi is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who completed a Doctor of Philosophy at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under M. A. Mehendale. She held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).

K. N. Jayatilleke (1920–1970) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera, Ludwig Wittgenstein, and at the University of Cambridge, later serving as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon (~1955–1963).

K. Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (attested 2008) and held a post at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020).

K. T. S. Sarao (born 1955) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed PhDs at the University of Delhi and Cambridge (under F. R. Allchin and K. R. Norman), becoming a Professor at Delhi in 1995.

K. V. Puttappa (1904–1994) was an Indian scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his education at Hardwick High School and College, Maharaja's College, Mysore, and the University of Mysore (~1927–1929).

K. V. Raman (1934–2024) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras, he served at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1957–1976) and was Professor and Head at Madras (1976–1995).

K. V. Ramesh (1935–2013) was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Director of the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1986–1987) and Honorary Director at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (attested 2012).

K. V. Sarma (1919–2005) was an Indologist and historian educated at the University of Kerala under V. A. Ramaswami Sastri. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute, Panjab University, and Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, later directing the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation.

K. Venkata Ramanan was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a Doctor of Letters at Visva-Bharati University, researched at Peking University (1947–1949) under Yongtong Tang and Sentian Wang, and later taught at Visva-Bharati University.
Kaigen Noritake is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kenyu Mitomo. He held an academic post as assistant professor (助教授) at Rissho University (attested 2007).

Kaikyoku Watanabe (1872–1933) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Strasbourg (PhD 1900–1907) under Ernst Leumann and held professorships at Shukyo, Toyo, Kokushikan, and Taisho Universities, also serving as principal of Shiba High School.

Kaiten Nukariya (1867–1934) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Sendan-Rin, Komazawa University, and Keio University. He lectured at Harvard and spent his career at Soto-shu/Komazawa University, serving as its first president from 1925 to 1934.
